instruction: In Y22-2119-assign4.docx, make all italic terms more visually distinct by changing their font size to 14pt and adding underline formatting to them. Save the file.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly identifies all italic runs (run.italic=True) and extracts both font size and underline properties for each run.
Metric correctly awards 0.5 partial credit for all italic runs being 14pt and 0.5 for all italic runs being underlined, covering both instruction requirements.
Postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring fresh file state is read.
Expected values (all_italic_size_14=true, all_italic_underlined=true) are semantically correct for the task requirements.
Minor issue: Getter iterates only doc.paragraphs, not doc.tables — italic text in table cells would be missed, potentially causing false negatives if the document contains italic text in tables.

Minor issue: run.font.size and run.font.underline return None for style-inherited formatting (not direct formatting); None values result in false negatives for those checks. However, since the expected completion method (Find & Replace) applies direct formatting, this is unlikely in practice.
Metric does not use the 'expected' parameter (logic is hardcoded), but the hardcoded thresholds match the rule values, so there is no semantic mismatch.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider also iterating through doc.tables (each cell's paragraphs) to capture italic runs in table cells for complete coverage.
When checking font size, handle None (style-inherited) by also checking the paragraph/style-level size as a fallback.
When checking underline, handle None (style-inherited) by checking the paragraph style or default character style for inherited underline.
